## How they got there
Inter finished as runner-up after losing the final to Paris Saint-Germain 0-5. Their profile during the league and group phases was defined by a points per game rate of 2.38, which placed them better than 94% of that season's group/league-phase teams, alongside an opponent shots on target per game of 2.9, ranking better than 89% of peers. They also recorded a goal difference per game of 1.25, performing better than 88% of the same pool of teams.

## Would the model have picked them?
The model assigned Inter a 12.9% probability of reaching the final, which exceeds the base rate of 8.3%, yet their rank among knockout teams was only seventh. Because the model selects a team only if it ranks in its top two, and any lower rank means it did not pick them even when the probability beat the base rate, the model would not have selected Inter for this stage. The nearest expected stage to the model's expectation of 0.87 on the knockout scale was quarter-finals.

## Weak spots
The team's least effective metrics were shot accuracy at 39.2%, where they were better than only 8% of that season's group/league-phase teams, and distance covered per game at 68.1 km, which beat just 3% of their peers. Although the model marked fouls committed per game (lower is better) as a factor pushing the prediction down most with a contribution of -0.08, Inter ranked well on this stat by beating 83% of that season's group/league-phase teams.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. Write them as 'better than X% of teams', never as 'top X%'. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat or a team's profile drove, powered, propelled, carried, helped, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
